docs.title: agents
docs.text:
Shared Claude Code rules and skills, and the status line.

git clone git@github.com:bnomis/agents.git ~/src/agents
~/src/agents/bin/install-claude.sh

The installer links the contents of claude/ into ~/.claude/, so the rules load in every Claude Code session and each skill becomes a slash command in every project. It also sets claude/statusline.py as the status line unless one is already set; see Command line and hooks.

The auditme checker, its pre-commit hooks, the Stop hook and /auditme-project-setup are in the auditor repository (bnomis/auditor, https://bnomis.github.io/auditor/).

docs.title: What is in the repository
docs.text: Path What it is claude/rules/ Rules loaded into every session: git, Python, reviews, security and the rest. See Rules. claude/skills/ Slash commands for specs, task lists, the TODO.md workflow, shipping and cleanup. See Skills. claude/statusline.py The Claude Code status line. bin/ The installer. See Command line and hooks.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
1. Read How it works for the moving parts and why each is where it is.
  2. Look things up in the reference: Skills, Rules and Command line and hooks.

docs.title: Why
docs.text:
• A rule a script can check is a hook. A rule that lives only in prose drifts; the checks that enforce the mechanical rules are run by the auditor repository's hooks (bnomis/auditor, https://bnomis.github.io/auditor/).
  • Nothing here is about one project. Rules, skills, fixtures and commit messages stay generic; a hook rejects any file or commit message that names a project from a list kept outside the repository.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The repository's consumer is Claude Code on your machine, which reads the rules and skills from ~/.claude/. The checker that enforces the mechanical rules in each project's pre-commit and CI is in the auditor repository (bnomis/auditor, https://bnomis.github.io/auditor/).

flowchart LR
    repo["agents repository"]
    home["~/.claude/<br>rules, skills, status line"]
    repo -- "bin/install-claude.sh<br>(symlinks)" --> home

docs.title: Rules and skills in ~/.claude/
docs.text:
bin/install-claude.sh links claude/ into ~/.claude/ one level down: a file such as claude/CLAUDE.md becomes a symlink, and a directory such as claude/skills/ becomes a real directory whose entries are symlinks, so skills and rules of your own in ~/.claude/ sit beside the shared ones. A file already at a link's place is renamed with an .orig suffix, never overwritten. Because the links point back into your clone, a git pull updates every session at once; only a new top-level entry (a new skill or rule) needs the installer run again.

  • Rules (claude/rules/) are Markdown files Claude Code loads as instructions. A rule with a paths: list in its front matter loads only when the session works on matching files.
  • Skills (claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md) are invoked as /<name>, or picked up by Claude when a request matches the skill's description.
  • claude/CLAUDE.md holds the working agreement loaded in every session: plan first, verify before calling work done, turn each correction into a rule.

These files are shared by every project, so none of them names one. A project's own rules and skills live in its own claude/ directory, loaded from that project's CLAUDE.md.

docs.title: Records in a repository
docs.text:
The skills keep their records in the repository they work on:

Path Written by Holds agents/specs/<slug>/spec.md /specdev a spec, with its version, status and amendments agents/tasks/<slug>/tasks-N.md /taskdev a task list for a spec, run task by task agents/tasks/order-<slug>.md /todo-run-order a run order of task lists, run by /rro TODO.md /todo-add, /todo-review, /todo-do open work only, in implementation order DONE.md /todo-do, /todo-review finished items, unchanged, each with a Done: line

See Skills for each skill's inputs and outputs.

docs.title: Command line and hooks
docs.text: Reference for the scripts in this repository and the hooks it runs. The auditme checker, the no-project-names check, their hooks and the Stop hook are documented in the auditor repository (bnomis/auditor, https://bnomis.github.io/auditor/reference/cli/).

docs.title: bin/install-claude.sh
docs.text:
bin/install-claude.sh [--dry-run] [any other install-in-claude option]

Links the contents of claude/ into ~/.claude/, and sets the status line, by running the shared installer install-in-claude at the commit pinned in the script's INSTALL_IN_CLAUDE_REV:

uvx --from "git+ssh://git@github.com/bnomis/install-in-claude.git@$INSTALL_IN_CLAUDE_REV" \
    install-in-claude --source "$REPO/claude" \
    --set-if-absent 'statusLine={"command":"~/.claude/statusline.py","type":"command"}'

Its own arguments pass through: bin/install-claude.sh --dry-run prints what would change and changes nothing. It needs uv, and SSH access to bnomis/install-in-claude for the first run of a pinned commit; uvx caches it after that.

What the installer does, in short (its README has the detail):

  • Checks every option and reads ~/.claude/settings.json first; a settings file that is not a valid JSON object stops it, exit 1, before anything is linked or written.
  • For each top-level entry of claude/ (dotfiles skipped): a file (CLAUDE.md, statusline.py) becomes a symlink in ~/.claude/; a directory (rules/, skills/) becomes a real directory in ~/.claude/ whose entries are symlinks, so ~/.claude/skills/shipit links to claude/skills/shipit/. Links are relative. An existing symlink is replaced; an existing file is renamed with a .orig suffix (numbered when that name is taken).
  • Prints any dangling symlinks in ~/.claude/ and its immediate subdirectories, with a quoted rm command to remove them. It does not remove them.
  • Sets statusLine to {"type": "command", "command": "~/.claude/statusline.py"} in ~/.claude/settings.json, unless a statusLine is already set, in which case it is left as it is. Every other key is kept; the first original is copied to settings.json.orig; the file is written atomically and keeps its mode.
Exit Meaning 0 Installed, or nothing to do 1 settings.json is not valid JSON or not a JSON object; nothing changed 2 A bad argument; nothing changed

Environment: HOME.

To upgrade the installer, set INSTALL_IN_CLAUDE_REV to a newer commit (git ls-remote git@github.com:bnomis/install-in-claude.git refs/heads/main, first field) and run bin/install-claude.sh --dry-run to see what it changes.

docs.title: claude/statusline.py
docs.text:
statusline.py < status.json

A Claude Code status line command. Reads the session's status JSON on stdin and prints one line of the available parts joined by |:

Part Source Model name model.display_name ctx: N% context_window.used_percentage 5h: N% rate_limits.five_hour.used_percentage cwd: <dir> workspace.current_dir git: <branch>+S~M git in the working directory: S files staged (green), M modified (yellow); omitted outside a repository

A missing, zero or wrongly typed field is left out. When stdin is empty or not a JSON object it prints an empty line. It writes nothing else and always exits 0. Environment: none.

The installer links it to ~/.claude/statusline.py and sets it as the status line, unless one is already set.

docs.title: Pre-commit hooks
docs.text: This repository publishes no hooks. Its .pre-commit-config.yaml pins auditme-changed, auditme-all (at [manual, pre-push]) and no-project-names from the auditor repository (bnomis/auditor, https://bnomis.github.io/auditor/reference/cli/), which documents each one. It also runs ruff-check, ruff-format and shellcheck from their own repositories.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text: A rule is a Markdown file of instructions that Claude Code loads into a session's context. The shared rules live in claude/rules/ and claude/rules/python/.

docs.title: How rules reach a session
docs.text:
bin/install-claude.sh links claude/rules/ into ~/.claude/rules/: each entry of claude/rules/ becomes a symlink there, so ~/.claude/rules/python is a link to claude/rules/python/. See Command line and hooks for the installer.

Claude Code reads ~/.claude/rules/ as user-level rules for every project. Nothing in claude/CLAUDE.md links to them; the rules directory alone is what loads them. Rules cross-reference each other with relative links (for example [security.md](security.md)). A rule from another repository is named by its installed path instead (~/.claude/rules/auditme/coding-standards.md): each installed directory is a symlink into its own repository, so a ../ link from it would be followed into that repository, not across to the other.

  • Unscoped rules (no frontmatter) load at the start of every session.

  • Path-scoped rules start with paths: frontmatter listing file globs, and load only when Claude works with a matching file:

    ---
paths:
  - "**/*.md"
---

    markdown.md and every rule under python/ are scoped this way. The Python rules match **/*.py; some add **/pyproject.toml, **/uv.lock, **/requirements.txt or **/bin/*.

A project's own rules do not go here. Per rule-scope.md, everything in claude/rules/ holds for any project; a rule for one project goes in that project's claude/rules/ (and its skills in claude/skills/), at the root of its workspace, loaded from the workspace's CLAUDE.md.

docs.title: General rules
docs.text: File Requires asking-questions.md Questions to the user go through the structured question tool, one decision per question, with clickable options and the recommendation first. bash-guidelines.md Non-interactive shell use: no pagers or editors, limit output with flags, judge multi-check commands by exit status, match processes by name, never pkill -f. counts-in-prose.md A number in prose is dropped, replaced by the command that produces it, or generated; dated measurements are exempt. design.md Per-input details (paths, column names, mappings) are required runtime config, never defaults; an inferred value needs positive evidence. environment.md Load environment variables with direnv from .envrc; do not edit .envrc unless told to. git-conventions.md Install pre-commit and pre-push hooks, make every script-checkable rule a hook, Conventional Commits, feature branches, no generated data in git, leave the user's own changes out of commits. identifiers-in-prose.md Decode every spec, review or task label (decision IDs, task numbers, hashes) in plain words wherever it appears in a message. locale.md British English spelling and grammar. markdown.md Plain ASCII punctuation in .md files, chat and commit messages: -, straight quotes, .... Scoped to **/*.md. reviews.md Anything the user must review is a review document in the repository plus an interactive page whose answers save as they are made. rule-scope.md Shared rules, skills and every other file in this repository (and any repository used across projects) name no project; project-specific rules go in the project's claude/ directory. security.md No secrets in the repository or in output; never list environment variables; no raw PII in shipped logs; repeat the secrets rule in every subagent brief. tools-and-libraries.md Prefer dependencies already in the project or the stdlib; check a library's maintenance status before recommending it, and give alternatives when flagging one. user-guides.md User guides cover install, configure, run, examples and trade-offs, and are updated in the same commit as user-visible behaviour. verify-claims.md A statement about current state comes from a check run for it, timed with date -u; absence is claimed only after a search by likely name. versions.md Record every version that shapes an output, check it wherever saved work is reused, refuse a mismatch, pin what is checked.

docs.title: Python rules
docs.text:
Every file here is path-scoped (see above).

File Requires python/argparse.md argparse only in unconverted code and standard-library-only scripts (every new CLI uses cappa), with a trailing comma in its calls so arguments format one per line. python/asserts.md No assert in product code; raise an exception. Tests may assert. python/environment.md Source bin/activate.sh, then run bin/ scripts and pytest directly, without uv run. python/logging.md ETA: log lines at info level, a format downstream tooling parses. python/testing.md Tests in src/tests/ mirroring the source; never the full suite routinely; scope runs to changed modules and their importers; mark slow tests; bound hypothesis examples. python/tools-and-libraries.md The standard toolset: uv, loguru, cappa, ruff, pytest, hypothesis, aiohttp, mypy, Docker. python/utilities.md Utility scripts in bin/, dash-separated names, each with a bash wrapper that sources bin/activate.sh.

docs.title: Rules from the auditor repository
docs.text: The Python rules the auditme checker enforces - coding-standards.md, imports.md and dependencies.md - live beside the checker in the auditor repository (bnomis/auditor), whose installer links them into ~/.claude/rules/auditme/. Its Rules page lists them, and maps each shared rule a hook or checker rule enforces to that check, including rule-scope.md, git-conventions.md and python/asserts.md from here. No hook or checker rule checks any rule it does not list.

docs.title: Skills
docs.text:
Each skill is a directory under claude/skills/<name>/ holding a SKILL.md and any scripts or templates it uses. bin/install-claude.sh links claude/ into ~/.claude/, so every skill is available in every project as ~/.claude/skills/<name>/.

Invoke a skill in Claude Code as /<name> [args], or by asking for what it does: the when_to_use list in each skill's frontmatter names the phrases that trigger it ("ship it", "add a todo").

The /auditme and /auditme-project-setup skills are in the auditor repository (bnomis/auditor, https://bnomis.github.io/auditor/reference/skills/).

Common behaviour:

  • The planning and TODO skills check git status first and ask whether to commit uncommitted changes before touching a file they own.
  • They ask before committing, and do not push unless asked. The exception is /shipit, whose job is to commit, merge and push.
  • Steps that change something outside the working tree (deleting branches, for example) are confirmed with the user first.
  • Questions to the user go through Claude Code's AskUserQuestion tool where the skill names it.

docs.title: Planning
docs.text: Skill Invocation Purpose specdev /specdev <spec-name> Write, review or update a spec; detect drift from the code taskdev /taskdev <spec-name-or-path> Turn a spec or review into an ordered task list testplan /testplan [scope] Find testing gaps and write a test plan

docs.title: TODO workflow
docs.text: Skill Invocation Purpose todo-add /todo-add [description] File one verified, dated finding in TODO.md, in order todo-review /todo-review Re-check, consolidate and reorder the whole of TODO.md todo-do /todo-do [item title] Do the first (or named) item, or start a spec for it todo-run-order /todo-run-order <items> [run order name] Turn chosen items into specs, task lists and an order file for /rro survey /survey [root] Survey every repository for unfinished plans, fixable failures, doable items and stale branches; file the findings test-log-review /test-log-review [root] [--glob PATTERN] Trace the failures and warnings in every repository's newest pytest logs; review page; file the approved fixes note-add /note-add [note] Append a dated, self-explanatory note to NOTES.md

docs.title: Git
docs.text: Skill Invocation Purpose shipit /shipit [message hint] Commit, merge the branch into main, push main cleanup /cleanup [repo-path] Delete local branches and worktrees already merged

docs.title: Other
docs.text: Skill Invocation Purpose paper-pdf-hunter /paper-pdf-hunter <list> <folder> Find and download paper PDFs by driving a browser

docs.title: /specdev
docs.text:
/specdev <SPEC-NAME>

With no argument, lists specs from agents/specs/index.md and asks which. The name is slugified (lowercase ASCII alphanumerics, spaces to hyphens, repeated hyphens collapsed): "C++ Parser v2.0" becomes c-parser-v20.

  • Reads: AGENTS.md, README.md, agents/specs/index.md, the spec, and the implementation at the spec's module location.
  • New spec: interviews the user, writes a draft from the template (Version, Status: proposed, Date, then Module location, API, Error handling, Implementation, Settings, External dependencies), and adds it to the index.
  • Existing spec: runs drift detection against the code when it exists, checks the spec against the template and validation criteria, and suggests changes. Drift findings are never resolved without the user choosing a direction for each one.
  • Stops for: interview answers; each drift item (update spec, update code, or skip); commit.
  • Writes: agents/specs/<slug>/spec.md, agents/specs/index.md. Commits only the spec file, with a message such as docs(specs): add error handling to <SLUG> spec.

One spec covers one repository and is self-contained; cross-repository work is one spec per repository.

docs.title: /taskdev
docs.text:
/taskdev <SPEC-NAME>
/taskdev <SPEC-PATH>

An argument containing / is a path. A path that is not agents/specs/<slug>/spec.md (an audit review or test plan, for example) is non-spec input: the slug is the parent directory's name, and tasks cite Source instead of Spec.

  • Reads: the spec and its sibling documents, agents/tasks/index.md, earlier agents/tasks/<slug>/tasks-*.md, and the code under src/ to mark work already done.
  • Writes: agents/tasks/<slug>/tasks-N.md (never overwrites; N increments) and agents/tasks/index.md.
  • Stops for: an ambiguous spec (offers /specdev first, or proceeds with caveats); tasks that need a user decision; review of the list; commit.

Each task carries status, priority, complexity, spec reference, subtasks, acceptance criteria, notes, and a Definition of Done naming the project's own check commands literally. Per-task checks are scoped to the changed files; the last task runs the whole-tree lint and the full affected-tests run, and sets the spec's status to implemented. No task edits another repository.

docs.title: /testplan
docs.text:
/testplan                 # every module under src/
/testplan <module-path>   # one module and its tests
/testplan <spec-name>     # a spec's implementation
  • Reads: AGENTS.md, the modules in scope and their tests (src/tests/), earlier plans in agents/test-plans/, and uv run pytest --co -q.
  • Writes: agents/test-plans/plan-N.md (never overwrites), capped at 20 recommendations, favouring branching logic, error paths and edge cases.
  • Then: if there are recommendations, runs /taskdev agents/test-plans/plan-N.md.
  • Stops for: commit (docs(tests): add plan-N).

docs.title: /todo-add
docs.text:
/todo-add <description>
/todo-add                 # files the finding just established in the conversation
  • Reads: the project's TODO.md convention section (in AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md), TODO.md in full, the tail of DONE.md, and the code needed to confirm the cause.
  • Writes: one item in TODO.md: a specific ## title, the dated finding (inside the project's accept markers), the cause with path:line, and a Fix direction. It is inserted in implementation order, never appended. A finding that shares a root cause with an open item joins it as a ### finding; one that touches several items is proposed as a consolidation first.
  • Stops for: uncommitted TODO.md changes; a proposed consolidation; commit (docs(todo): ...).

A fix that belongs to another repository is filed in that repository's TODO.md. Conventions shared by the TODO skills are in claude/skills/todo-review/conventions.md; a project's own TODO.md section overrides them.

docs.title: /todo-review
docs.text:
/todo-review
  • Reads: TODO.md, DONE.md, and the project's specs, task lists, reviews, code markers (TODO, FIXME, expected failures) and recent commit bodies, looking for promised work no item records.
  • Proposes, before any edit: items to move to DONE.md with evidence, stale premises, missing items, groups sharing a root cause, and the new order, shown as a table.
  • Writes, once confirmed: TODO.md reordered and consolidated (original bodies kept verbatim under ###), finished items appended to DONE.md with a Done: line, missing items added, stale premises corrected with a dated note.
  • Verifies: saves HEAD:TODO.md to a scratch file first, then runs python3 ~/.claude/skills/todo-review/verify_bodies.py <before> TODO.md DONE.md, which exits non-zero if any original item body is lost or altered.
  • Stops for: uncommitted TODO.md changes; the proposal; commit (docs(todo): ...).

Order, highest first: work-losing defects, blockers, waste, features (each before what it makes cheaper or safer), then deferred items.

docs.title: /todo-do
docs.text:
/todo-do
/todo-do <item title>

Re-checks the item is still open, still true, and not one symptom of a shared cause (if it is, proposes /todo-review and stops). Then sizes it:

Size Condition Action Small One logical change; no artefact, contract or public API change; no spec section rewrite; no paid run or real-data change Fix on a branch, test first for defects, run the project's checks, move the item to DONE.md with a Done: line, add dated notes to other items whose path:line moved Large Anything else, or the item says it goes through a spec Run /specdev, stop for spec review, offer /taskdev, add a Spec: ...; tasks: ... line to the item; it moves to DONE.md when the task list finishes
  • Stops for: a done or stale item; a shared cause; spec review; a paid LLM run (asks for provider and a cost estimate); commit.
  • Backs up real project artefacts before a run that rewrites them; a new defect found mid-run is filed with /todo-add, not fixed in place.

docs.title: /todo-run-order
docs.text:
/todo-run-order <items> [run order name]

<items> picks TODO.md items by position, counting ## headings from 1, as numbers and ranges: 1-3,5,8. Starts from the main checkout on a clean default branch level with its remote.

  • Re-checks each item as /todo-do does, sizes it, and plans a task list per small item and one or more specs per large one, each in this repository.
  • Writes the specs with /specdev, then one review of all of them, agents/reviews/order-<slug>-specs.md, with its page, naming every prerequisite the operator must provide; stops until it is answered.
  • Writes a task list per spec with /taskdev. Each list's last task saves its final test output where /rro's merge gate reads it, and each item gets its Spec: ...; tasks: ... line.
  • Writes agents/tasks/order-<slug>.md, taking the settings from the newest order file or the project's rules, and checks it with /rro's parser.
  • Stops for: a done, stale or shared-cause item; the specs' review; a required setting nothing gives; commit. It never starts the order.

docs.title: /survey
docs.text:
/survey [root]

Answers, for every repository at and below the root: which specs and task lists are not implemented, which expected failures and known bugs could be fixed, which TODO.md items can be done now, and which branches and worktrees are stale.

  • Runs: python3 ~/.claude/skills/survey/inventory.py <root>, which prints each repository's status, worktrees, branches (merged or not), task lists with open tasks and specs not marked implemented. Then one read-only subagent per large repository, or per group of small ones, reads TODO.md, test markers, reviews and specs.
  • Reports under the five questions, after checking in the code every finding it recommends acting on. Repository state is given with the time it was checked.
  • Files, on request: each finding in the TODO.md of the repository where its fix is made, by the todo-add conventions. A finding blocked on an upstream release, people (labelling, native readers), data or a deferred decision is filed as deferred; an item already fixed moves to DONE.md.
  • Hands over: the changed files, a table of what was filed, and an implementation order saying what can run in parallel.
  • Stops for: the request to file; commit (docs(todo): ..., one per repository). It never deletes branches (that is /cleanup) or pushes.

docs.title: /test-log-review
docs.text:
/test-log-review [root] [--glob PATTERN]

Reads the newest pytest log of each kind (a full run, a correctness run) in every repository at and below the root, and turns its failures and warnings into reviewed, filed work.

  • Runs: python3 ~/.claude/skills/test-log-review/scan.py <root>, which prints each log's summary line, its FAILED and ERROR lines and its warnings grouped by message, counting from pytest's own summary line. Then read-only subagents trace each warning to its source: one for third-party warnings shared across repositories, one per repository or group for the rest.
  • Reviews: a review document and an interactive page built from page-template.html and checked with check-page.js: real defects, test-side fixes and third-party warnings to approve or flag, and decisions for fixes that change output or upgrade a recorded dependency.
  • Files, after the answers: each approved fix in the TODO.md of the repository where it is made, by the todo-add conventions, with any correction a filing agent finds recorded in the review.
  • Hands over: an implementation order in waves, a shared-environment change first and alone.
  • Stops for: the review's answers; commit (docs(todo): ..., one per repository). It never runs the test suite or pushes.

docs.title: /note-add
docs.text:
/note-add <the note>
/note-add                 # asks what to note
  • Reads: NOTES.md in the repository root (offers to create it), and the repository to fill in missing context.
  • Writes: appends one note to NOTES.md:
## <short title>

Added YYYY-MM-DD. <the note>

Adds to an existing note on the same subject instead of duplicating it. Never edits other notes. - Stops for: up to a few clarifying questions on what a later reader would miss (what, why, where, when, who); a preview with add / change / cancel; commit (docs(notes): <subject>).

Open work with a cause belongs in TODO.md; the skill redirects to /todo-add.

docs.title: /shipit
docs.text:
/shipit [commit message hint]

It is not called /ship: Claude Code has a built-in /ship (commit, open a pull request and watch it), and a skill of the same name is hidden behind it.

  1. Inspects git status, diffs, branch, worktrees and recent log; stops if it sees secrets, build output, large binaries or unrelated changes.
  2. Commits by logical change, staging files by name, with conventional commit messages; fixes hook failures rather than bypassing them.
  3. On a feature branch: fetches, rebases onto origin/main, and fast-forwards main (in the worktree that holds main, if another one does).
  4. Pushes main, after git pull --rebase if origin/main moved. Never force-pushes; stops on rejection.
  5. Reports the commits, the merge and the push, with repository state stated only from a fresh git fetch and git status -sb.

Feature branches and worktrees are left in place; use /cleanup.

docs.title: /cleanup
docs.text:
/cleanup [repo-path]

Works on one repository (default: the current one) and all its worktrees; never changes the remote. It reads only until the plan is approved.

  • Merged means, against the local default branch or origin/<default>: ancestry, a rebase merge (git cherry shows no +), or a squash merge (a probe commit of the branch's tree shows no +).
  • Removes: prunable worktrees; clean worktrees whose branch or detached HEAD is merged; merged local branches. Skips the main worktree, the current one, locked or dirty worktrees, and worktrees holding a submodule (for which it prints the commands to run by hand).
  • Stops for: one approval of the plan - all, a named subset, or cancel. The plan lists ignored files each worktree removal will delete.
  • Never --force on worktrees. Uses git branch -D only for a branch it proved merged by the rebase or squash test.

docs.title: /paper-pdf-hunter
docs.text:
/paper-pdf-hunter <PAPER-LIST> <OUTPUT-FOLDER>

Drives a real browser (Claude in Chrome preferred, else Playwright MCP; stops if neither is connected) to find a PDF for each paper in a Markdown list. It does not use scholarly APIs.

  • Reads: the Markdown list in any citation shape, extracting title, authors, year, DOI, arXiv ID and URLs.
  • Searches, stopping at the first verified PDF: arXiv or DOI landing page, Google Scholar (including all versions), preprint and repository sites, general web search, then public ResearchGate or Academia.edu copies. Shadow libraries and paywall bypasses are out of scope.
  • Verifies each file: %PDF header, size, and title on the first pages via pdftotext.
  • Writes: <FirstAuthor>_<Year>_<first-five-title-words>.pdf (with _preprint or _accepted suffixes, never overwriting) and download_report.md in the output folder. Output defaults to ./papers/ beside the list.
  • Stops for: a missing list or folder, Chrome's PDF download setting, CAPTCHAs (the user solves them), and any login it would have to perform on the user's behalf.
